summary: Trace an actual blocked request to its current owner and inspect a cycle witness under explicit assumptions.
objective: Build a deadlock inspector for exclusive single-instance resources where requests create wait-for edges and I can inspect the resulting cycle.
intent_signals: Build a deadlock inspector for exclusive single-instance resources where requests create wait-for edges and I can inspect the resulting cycle.
example_prompts: Build a deadlock inspector for exclusive single-instance resources where requests create wait-for edges and I can inspect the resulting cycle.
negative_signals: No multiple instances, OR-waits, preemptive locks, reentrant self-requests, distributed snapshots or starvation/fairness diagnosis. Recovery abort is an explicit intervention, never an ordinary progress step.
not_for: No multiple instances, OR-waits, preemptive locks, reentrant self-requests, distributed snapshots or starvation/fairness diagnosis. Recovery abort is an explicit intervention, never an ordinary progress step.

entities.name: Process and resource cards
entities.guidance: Offer linked views: resource-allocation edges P→R for requests and R→P for ownership, alongside the contracted process-only graph. Z separates the two named views; it is not waiting time.

entities.name: Cycle witness
entities.guidance: Number cycle edges and show the underlying request/resource/owner evidence; distinguish cycle members from processes blocked upstream.

state_contract.model: Finite processes/resources; one nonpreemptible exclusive instance per resource; owner[r] is null or one process, and each blocked process has one outstanding request. A blocked process cannot release while waiting. Before accepting a request, reject owner[r]=p visibly without changing ownership or outstanding requests. For an accepted request[p]=r owned by q≠p, derive edge p→q. Detect directed cycles from this current snapshot, not from historical trails.
state_contract.authority: The typed domain model owns each committed state and result. Geometry, labels and selection derive from that model; animation cannot certify a claim.
actions: Let an unblocked process request a resource; grant if free or record a blocking request.
Release only from an unblocked owner; grant a newly freed resource by a declared deterministic queue rule.
Load P1 owns R1 and waits R2 while P2 owns R2 and waits R1; inspect cycle or explicitly abort a selected process as recovery.

invariants: Every wait-for edge must resolve to a current blocked request and current owner; removing ownership must remove or recompute the edge.
A two-process circular wait gives a cycle witness; a chain ending at an unblocked owner does not.
Reject a multiple-instance input in this mode. A cycle criterion cannot silently transfer to a general resource-allocation system.
If P owns R and requests R, report an unsupported self-request and leave ownership/request state unchanged; do not silently block P while omitting its self-cycle.
motion_guidance: Step commits one semantic action; pause freezes presentation and leaves the committed state inspectable. Reset cancels pending playback and restores the complete starting state.
Offer a static transition highlight and an equivalent readable table for reduced motion. Camera travel is presentation, not an inference or domain operation.
creative_affordances: Use shallow sculptural cards, restrained materials and selective focus to expose relationships. Prefer a flat readable layout whenever depth has no declared role.
known_limits: No multiple instances, OR-waits, preemptive locks, reentrant self-requests, distributed snapshots or starvation/fairness diagnosis. Recovery abort is an explicit intervention, never an ordinary progress step.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no generated artifact, solver integration, runtime behavior or visual check has run.

physical_contract.scope: Abstract symbols and logical state; mesh contact, light and motion have no causal role in the model.

object_craft.structure: Offer linked views: resource-allocation edges P→R for requests and R→P for ownership, alongside the contracted process-only graph. Z separates the two named views; it is not waiting time.
object_craft.material: Matte surfaces and high-contrast labels; distinguish status with text and border style as well as color.

claims.statement: With one instance per resource type, a wait-for edge points from a waiting process to the process holding its requested resource, and a directed wait-for cycle indicates deadlock.
claims.scope: Exclusive, nonpreemptible single-instance resources and blocking waits in a consistent current snapshot.
